newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.08 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.08 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.08 percent to close at 1.0401 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band of 1.0400 to 1.0450 per dollar, dealers said.
"Because everybody was expecting a change in the mini-band today, the market was calm after the Central Bank's move," one trader said.

The Central Bank lowered the mini-band 0.1 percent by buying dollars at 1.0400 and selling at 1.0450 reais in a morning auction. The previous mini-band was set on December 31 between 1.039 and 1.044 reais to the dollar.

In addition, the bank sold 550 million of dollar-indexed National Treasury Notes (NTN-D) in a move to calm the dollar futures markets. The markets have been nervous over speculation that December's trade gap could rise to $1.5 billion.
The NTN-D auction and the lowering of the mini-band by just 0.1 percent were seen as signals that the Central Bank would maintain its current foreign exchange policy, dealers said.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.09 percent to end at 1.0457 to the dollar, following the drop in the mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.120 per greenback, traders said.
